hints: Look at each test as a clue about a functional group, starting with what Tollens' reagent and sodium each detect.
The yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ is the iodoform test, which is positive only for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group.
Combine the three clues together, a non-aldehyde with the iodoform group but with no $\text{O-H}$ group to react with sodium, to pick the one structure that fits all.
walkthrough:
**Interpret the Tollens' test**

Tollens' reagent is a mild oxidising agent that oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, giving a silver mirror. Ketones, esters and alcohols do not react.

Since X does not react, X is not an aldehyde. This rules out $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$.

**Interpret the iodoform test**

A yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ means a positive tri-iodomethane test.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This is given by methyl ketones, $\text{CH}_3\text{COR}$, and by the related secondary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)R}$. Ethanal also gives it, but it is already ruled out. An ester like $\text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$ does not give it.

**Interpret the sodium test**

Sodium reacts with compounds containing an acidic $\text{O-H}$ group, such as alcohols and carboxylic acids, to release hydrogen.

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$
Since X does not react with sodium, X has no $\text{-OH}$ group. This rules out the alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CHOHCH}_3$.

**Put the clues together**

X must be a non-aldehyde, iodoform-positive, and $\text{O-H}$ free. That perfectly matches a methyl ketone.

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is butan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so it gives $\text{CHI}_3$, but as a ketone it gives no Tollens' reaction and no reaction with Na.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ is ethanal, an aldehyde. It would give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent, so it fails the first clue, even though it does give a yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate because it contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ type structure.
options.B: Correct. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is butan-2-one, a methyl ketone. As a ketone it does not react with Tollens' reagent, its $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group gives a yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2$, and with no $\text{O-H}$ group it does not react with sodium.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$ is ethyl ethanoate, an ester. Esters do not react with Tollens' reagent and do not react with sodium, but they do not give the iodoform reaction, so no yellow precipitate would form. Students sometimes confuse the $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}-$ part with a methyl ketone.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHOHCH}_3$ is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so it does give a yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate and gives no Tollens' reaction. However, its $\text{-OH}$ group would react with sodium to give $\text{H}_2$, so it fails the third clue.
